answers.Q1: Compile-time (static) polymorphism - Achieved through function overloading and operator overloading.
answers.Q2:
Runtime (dynamic) polymorphism - Achieved through method overriding using virtual functions.

Advantages - Flexibility, code reusability and easy maintenance.
answers.Q3:
Polymorphism means "many forms" & allows the same function or method to perform different operations depending on the object or parameters, making programs more flexible and reusable.

Types -
answers.Q4:
Q class - A class is a user-defined datatype or blueprint used to create objects. It contains data member variables and member functions (methods) that define the properties and behaviour of object. A class does not occupy memory until an object is created.

Object - An object is an instance of class. It is a real-time (world) entity that occupies memory and can access the data members and functions defined in the class. Multiple objects can be created from a single class, each having its own state and behaviour.
